itinerary.cal: The CJ Couloir is best climbed early-season while still consolidated snow — by mid/late summer the Sill Glacier breaks up and it gets discontinuous and rockier; get a North Cascades NP wilderness permit for the overnight bivy.

days.note: From the Cascade Pass trailhead (verify Cascade River Road status first — it washes out periodically), walk back to the hairpin, scramble down, cross the creek, and bushwhack about 15 minutes to the base of the CJ Couloir. Climb roughly 3,400 ft of snow/ice — best done in the cold pre-dawn hours when it's frozen and rockfall risk from Johannesburg is lowest — to reach the C-J col and bivy on the snow there.
days.title: Approach and CJ Couloir to a col bivy

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Alpine start to be on the couloir while it's still frozen.

schedule.label: Reach base of CJ Couloir
schedule.detail: After the hairpin, creek crossing, and brush bushwhack.

schedule.label: Climb the CJ Couloir
schedule.detail: ~3,400 ft of snow/ice; fast light parties do it in ~3.25 hrs, expect 4+ with overnight packs.

schedule.label: Top out at C-J col
schedule.detail: Find a bivy site on the snow near the col.

schedule.label: Rest and rack up at camp
schedule.detail: Rehydrate and nap through the heat of the day; sort gear for tomorrow's pitches.

days.objective: Reach the Cascade-Johannesburg col via the CJ Couloir before the day warms

days.note: Traverse from the col to the base of Cascade Peak's NW Chimney in the moat and climb the roughly 3-pitch route (loose crux crack, then a cleaner 5.8 chimney, then a short loose pitch and simul-climbing to the summit). Rappel the route back to the moat, return to the col, break camp, then reverse the CJ Couloir and hike out — a long, full day.
days.title: NW Chimney to the summit, then out

schedule.label: Leave col camp
schedule.detail: Light rack for the climb; some parties cache overnight gear at the col and grab it on the way down.

schedule.label: Start climbing NW Chimney
schedule.detail: From the moat below the col; loose crux crack pitch first.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: After the 5.8 chimney pitch and a final loose/simul pitch.

schedule.label: Finish rappelling back to the col
schedule.detail: ~3 rappels down the route, building gear anchors as you go.

schedule.label: Break camp, reverse the couloir
schedule.detail: Descend the CJ Couloir; snow is softer and rockfall risk higher than the morning ascent, so move deliberately.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: ~12 hrs car-to-car-again on day 2.

days.objective: Climb the East Ridge/NW Chimney and descend all the way to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day round trip: ~3,400 ft of snow/ice up the CJ Couloir to a col bivy on day 1, then a long ~12-hr day 2 combining 3 technical pitches (5.8 chimney) with a full descent back to the car — about 4,200 ft total gain and 11+ miles round trip.

road.name: Cascade River Road
road.status: Closed to vehicles at Eldorado (milepost 20) as of early summer 2026 due to flood/landslide damage, adding roughly 4 miles one-way (8 miles round trip) of road walking or biking to reach the Cascade Pass trailhead. Check current NPS conditions before you go.
road.driveNote: From Marblemount, Cascade River Road runs paved then gravel out to the Cascade Pass trailhead (about 5 miles beyond the park boundary, 4 miles beyond the Eldorado parking area). The final 3 miles beyond Eldorado are narrow with steep drop-offs and are prone to ruts and washouts that need a high-clearance vehicle even in a normal year.
road.seasonalGate: Typically opens to the Cascade Pass trailhead parking area by late June, occasionally slipping into early July after a heavy snow year; the road is also subject to off-season winter closures and storm-damage closures like the 2026 Eldorado gate closure.

itinerary.cal: Pick up your Sahale Glacier/Horseshoe Basin camping permit at the Marblemount Ranger Station since sites can fill on summer weekends.

days.note: From the Cascade Pass Trailhead, climb switchbacks to Cascade Pass (5,400 ft, 3.7 mi) then continue up the Sahale Arm Trail to the permitted Sahale Glacier Camp at 7,600 ft. Most parties treat this as a half-day carry so they're fresh for an early alpine start the next morning.
days.title: Approach to Sahale Glacier Camp
days.objective: Reach Sahale Glacier Camp (7,600 ft) as base for the Horseshoe/Buckner traverse

days.note: Alpine start down off Sahale Arm into Horseshoe Basin, crossing snow/talus past old Davenport Mine relics to the base of Horseshoe's summit block. A short, exposed 5.2 step (rope, light rack, 30-60m) gains the true summit; most parties downclimb or make one short rappel back to the ledge. After returning to camp, break it down and hike the full ~5.7 mi / 4,000 ft back down to the trailhead the same day, making for a long but standard second day.
days.title: Summit push and full exit

schedule.label: Leave Sahale Glacier Camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start to be off the summit block before afternoon weather builds.

schedule.label: Drop into Horseshoe Basin
schedule.detail: Cross snowfield/talus below the Sahale-Buckner col, using old mining remains as landmarks.

schedule.label: Reach base of Horseshoe's summit block
schedule.detail: Scramble Class 3-4 terrain up the snowfield to the final rock step.

schedule.label: Rope up for the 5.2 crux
schedule.detail: Short technical pitch to the true summit; many parties solo-belay or simul with a light rack.

schedule.label: Summit, then downclimb/rappel
schedule.detail: Reverse the crux to the ledge below, then retrace the basin traverse to camp.

schedule.label: Back at Sahale Glacier Camp
schedule.detail: Break camp and continue the ~4,000 ft, 5.7 mi descent to the trailhead, typically finishing by early evening.

days.objective: Climb Horseshoe Peak via Horseshoe Basin, then break camp and hike all the way out

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip is the norm: ~5.7 mi/4,000 ft up to Sahale Glacier Camp on Day 1, then a long ~9-10 hr, ~9 mi summit-and-exit Day 2 with a short roped 5.2 step near the top; very fit parties do climb it car-to-car in a single ~12-16 hr day instead.

road.name: Cascade River Road
road.status: Open: the June 2026 closure to vehicles at Eldorado (milepost 20) for flooding/landslide damage has been lifted, and the park's road-conditions page, updated July 3, 2026, lists the road open.
road.driveNote: Gravel/paved, not suitable for sedans or low-clearance vehicles even when fully open; no RVs, large trailers, or vehicles over 22 ft. Road-end (Cascade Pass TH) sits at 3,660 ft, about 23 miles from Marblemount/Hwy 20.
road.seasonalGate: Typically opens to the Cascade Pass trailhead by late June each year (snowpack-dependent) and closes for the season with the first heavy snow.

itinerary.cal: Cache Col holds consolidated snow well into summer, so most parties do this in July-September when the col crossing is firm but not icy.

days.note: Hike the maintained Cascade Pass Trail to Cascade Pass, then leave the trail and climb cross-country over the Cache Glacier remnant to Cache Col before dropping about a mile to camp at Kool-Aid Lake, a small tarn at ~6,120 ft. This stretch is mostly on snow into midsummer and is the crux of the day more from routefinding/snow travel than distance.
days.title: Approach to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Reach high camp at Kool-Aid Lake

days.note: An early start lets you climb the peak on firm snow before it softens: cross the steep snow band near 7,100 ft and take a gully up to the summit ridge, then follow the ridge past a false summit to the true 7,821 ft top. Back at camp by mid-morning, most parties break camp and hike all the way out the same day rather than adding a third night.
days.title: Climb Hurry-Up Peak, then hike out

schedule.label: Leave Kool-Aid Lake camp
schedule.detail: Early start for firm snow on the col approach.

schedule.label: Reach the summit ridge
schedule.detail: Across the snow band near 7,100 ft and up a gully.

schedule.label: Summit along the ridge
schedule.detail: Scramble past a false summit to the true 7,821 ft top.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break camp, filter water, repack for the hike out.

schedule.label: Begin the hike out
schedule.detail: Re-cross Cache Col and descend past Cascade Pass.

schedule.label: Back at the trailhead
schedule.detail: Roughly 3,000 ft of net descent from camp to the car.

days.objective: Tag the summit via the South Ridge and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night trip: about 16 miles round trip with roughly 5,500 ft of total gain, mostly spent covering the Cascade Pass-Cache Col approach rather than the short summit scramble itself.

road.name: Cascade River Road (Forest Road 15)
road.status: Open: the June 2026 closure to vehicles at Eldorado/milepost 20 for flooding/landslide damage has been lifted, and the park's road-conditions page, updated July 3, 2026, lists the road open.
road.driveNote: 22.3 miles of paved/gravel road from Marblemount to the Cascade Pass Trailhead when fully open; add roughly 6 miles round trip on foot or bike whenever the road is gated at milepost 20.
road.seasonalGate: Typically gated for winter beyond a lower point on the road; check NPS road-conditions page for current mile-by-mile status.
